subject: matamata turtle
title: This Turtle Catches Fish Faster Than You Can Blink

scenes.text: This turtle can't chase fish. It doesn't need to.
The matamata lies still on a South American riverbed, disguised as a pile of dead leaves.
When a fish drifts close, its throat suddenly balloons open.
Water rushes in like a vacuum, and the fish goes with it. The lunge takes about twenty milliseconds.
A blink takes ten times longer. The turtle can't chew, so it swallows the fish whole.
Then it pushes the water back out, and waits for the next one.

description:
The matamata turtle of South America waits motionless on the riverbed and catches fish by suction: it suddenly expands its throat so water and prey rush into its mouth.
Studies filmed the strike engulfing prey within about 20 milliseconds, and the fish is swallowed whole.
Which turtle should we cover next?
first_comment: It even breathes through a snorkel-like snout without moving. Would you spot one in a river?
